chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you, a man from my brethren, a matter reaches me about him which I dislike, so I ask him about it and he denies it, and reliable people have informed me about him.'

He said to me: 'O Muhammad, deny your hearing and your sight regarding your brother. Even if fifty have testified in your presence under oath, and he says something to you, believe him and disbelieve them. Do not publicize anything about him that would disgrace him and destroy his magnanimity.'
So you will be among those about whom Allah said in His Book: 'Surely those who love that scandal should circulate respecting those who believe, they shall have a grievous chastisement.'
ai.seo_question: How should one handle negative reports about a brother in faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of innocence) in interpersonal relations, instructing believers to accept a brother's denial even against numerous reliable witnesses, thereby protecting his honor (*mur'ah*). This directive emphasizes avoiding the public exposure of faults (*kaff al-ayn*) to prevent the erosion of social dignity, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights of the individual over the community. The narration explicitly links this social ethic to the Quranic warning against those who delight in the spread of indecency, reinforcing the spiritual consequence of public shaming.
